operations.name: The kept lacuna
operations.work: If Not, Winter: Fragments of Sappho
operations.statement: **O1 — The kept lacuna.** *If Not, Winter: Fragments of Sappho* (2002) prints Sappho's fragments with the damage visible: brackets and white space where the papyrus is lost. The gap is set on the page as part of what reaches the reader. Carson's phrase for the brackets: "an aesthetic gesture toward the papyrological event" (Q1, through #625 §4 and #902). The archive reads the absence as "part of the transmission" (#625), sets Carson, who "leaves the wound open", beside a poet who fills the gaps (#562), records that she preserves fragment 31's fragmentary syntax (#337 §6.3) and its fifth-stanza opening (#1054), drawn like every modern edition from one manuscript stemma (#1052). Grade: Q1; archive reading. The Academy calls the book "her interpretation of Sappho's poem fragments" and counts the translations "independent works in their own right"; it says nothing of the gaps. Field: the book is listed (F21).
operations.grade: Q1; archive reading. The Academy calls the book "her interpretation of Sappho's poem fragments" and counts the translations "independent works in their own right"; it says nothing of the gaps. Field: the book is listed (F21).
operations.lost: the papyrus, the damage kept, Sappho

operations.name: The triangle of desire
operations.statement: **O2 — The triangle of desire.** *Eros the Bittersweet* (1986), a reworking of her 1981 doctoral thesis (F11), examines eros as pleasure and pain at once, after Sappho's *glukupikron* (F9), and "considers how triangulations of desire appear in the writings of Sappho, ancient Greek novelists, and Plato" (F10). Her formulation: "Where eros is lack, its activation calls for three structural components — lover, beloved, and that which comes between them" (Q1, through #626 §II). The Academy quotes her "stereoscopic vision" that can "hold in equipoise two perspectives at once" (Q1, through the biobibliography). A philological reading of a fragment becomes an instrument for reading desire. Grade: Q1; field; Academy.
operations.lost: the fragment, lack, pain with sweetness

operations.name: The philologist's procedure carried into the poem
operations.statement: **O3 — The philologist's procedure carried into the poem.** The Academy: "Almost all her literary production has centred upon the intersection between the philologist's obsession with words and the poet's desire for new meaning", and she "has herself identified the etymology of words as the starting point for all her work" (Academy). The thesis became an essay that, on John D'Agata's account, "first stunned the classics community as a work of Greek scholarship; then it stunned the nonfiction community … and then, and only then … it finally stunned the poets" (F12). Her books blend poetry, essay, prose, criticism, translation, dramatic dialogue, fiction and non-fiction (F8). The field records the dispute this produces: Kirsch, "The writing is clearly prose" (F34); D'Agata, how prosaic a poem can be "before it becomes something else altogether" (F35). Grade: Academy; field.

operations.name: The received figure given the whole book
operations.statement: **O4 — The received figure given the whole book.** *Autobiography of Red* (1998) takes as its starting point Stesichoros's fragments on the red winged Geryon, whom Herakles kills in his tenth labour for his cattle (F32; Academy). Carson "recasts the terrifying giant as a tender 'hero' devoted to his mother, in what becomes a modern Bildungsroman" (Academy); "In Carson, Herakles breaks Geryon's heart and steals his innocence" (Kirsch, F33). The figure at the edge of a hero's labour is given the whole book as its life. Grade: field; Academy; the Stesichorean base to read.
operations.grade: field; Academy; the Stesichorean base to read.
operations.lost: Stesichoros, Geryon, the life told whole
operations.caution: **Caution on O4.** The surviving fragments of Stesichoros's *Geryoneis* already give Geryon speech and pathos, his mother pleading with him (Q2, a reader's report of 8 October; to read: the fragments). O4 is stated at what Carson adds: the figure becomes the book's centre and its life is told whole. If a reading of the fragments finds that they already give Geryon a whole life, O4 is revised.

operations.name: The change of carrier
operations.statement: **O5 — The change of carrier.** *Nox* (2010), made in 2000 as an epitaph for her brother (F23), is "a creation as sculptural as it is literary, an epitaph in the form of a box containing an accordion-fold-out of pictures, letters and other written texts", with Catullus's elegy 101 for his brother and "Carson's moving translation of the poem" (Academy); its design and performance were done with Robert Currie (F24). The elegy is set in the object that carries it, and the ancient elegy for a brother is carried inside the modern one. Grade: Academy; field; attested by the author, who read the object in his own copy (the box, the fold-out, Catullus 101 and its translation "all check out", 8 October 2026; the copy is no longer held). Pointer: the conclusion of the author's 2013 dissertation, *Strange New Canons*, treats *Nox* (#921 §2.7 reports the pairing with "Snub-Poemed"); it is unread in this round and enters O5 as an archive reading when read.
operations.grade: Academy; field; attested by the author, who read the object in his own copy (the box, the fold-out, Catullus 101 and its translation "all check out", 8 October 2026; the copy is no longer held). Pointer: the conclusion of the author's 2013 dissertation, *Strange New Canons*, treats *Nox* (#921 §2.7 reports the pairing with "Snub-Poemed"); it is unread in this round and enters O5 as an archive reading when read.
operations.lost: the elegy, the brother, Catullus 101, the box

operations.name: The translation as the fragment's vehicle
operations.statement: 3.2 **R1 — The translation as the fragment's vehicle.** Fragment 147's contemporary circulation "is overwhelmingly Carson-mediated" (*If Not, Winter*: "someone will remember us / I say / even in another time"), in epigraphs, memorial culture and reflective sites, and the AI Overview's remembrance card composes from that register (#1548 §6; Q1, documented from the search surface). It is an operation of a different kind: performed by the work in other hands, after it left the author's, and kept apart from O1–O5 for that reason. It has a twin in this object: Carson's translation carries Sappho, keeping the gap; the motivation now carries Carson (§5.3).
operations.kept_at_motivation_grain: a relation to translation, at most
operations.lost: fragment 147, Carson's English as its carrier

operations.name: the relation the work bears to the classical tradition
operations.statement: Of the five compositional operations, four are addressed to the classical text at a different stage of its transmission: kept damaged (O1), read into a structure of desire (O2), given a whole book (O4), carried inside another elegy and its object (O5). The fifth carries the philologist's procedure into the poem (O3). The relation the work bears to the classical tradition, on this specification, is to the text *as transmitted*: quoted, damaged, lost, translated, and surviving in the form of its survival.

candidates.name: James Dooley
candidates.statement: **James Dooley.** On 31 August 2026 a fabricated coronation story was published presenting Dooley as crowned "King of AEO" at Leigh Sports Village, in a ceremony led by Jesper Nissen. No such ceremony occurred. Edward Sturm, observing from outside the contest, records that Nissen "made up an official ceremony taking place in a big stadium," that Dooley set out "to show up #1 on Google for 'king of AEO', a keyword that nobody was targeting or cared about," and that "the AI Overview initially treated 'King of AEO' as a real title and repeated that Jesper's made-up event actually happened – based only on what the press releases said." The releases were syndicated to press-release networks including USA Today's and Barchart's. Oliveira's cross-locale record has the US AI Overview naming Dooley "most prominently recognized."

candidates.name: David G. Quaid
candidates.statement: **David G. Quaid.** Entered 4 September with LinkedIn articles, video and the exact-match domain kingofaeo.co; the US and Brazilian AI Overviews in Oliveira's record list him.

candidates.name: Vithurs
candidates.statement: **Vithurs.** A press release of 7 September announced Vithurs as named by "a private vote conducted through social media," which it said "is not presented as an accreditation or award issued by an industry governing body," and pointed to a site monitoring "how different systems respond to searches and questions relating to Vithurs, Answer Engine Optimization and the King of AEO title." A network of eleven domains carries the relation. Reported from the project's own pages (unverified; see Evidence Membrane): sixteen queries across eight platforms fixed in advance; a twelve-field observation record; no rerolling of favourable answers; null results kept; the experimenter disclosed as the subject; the eleven domains counted as one source, "the same voice in a different typeface"; syndication named as inflating source counts; and a falsification threshold set before testing, three of six answer engines on two dates at least 21 days apart in clean sessions, distinguishing the project's title statement from the empirical claim that engines name Vithurs.

candidates.name: Stephane Morera
candidates.statement: **Stephane Morera.** Entered 13 September with baseline measurements and predictions published before results (EVOIX).

candidates.name: Allan Oliveira
candidates.statement: **Allan Oliveira.** Entered 17 September; built a claimant index, timeline and cross-engine, cross-locale record, and applied his rubric to his own claim. The Brazilian AI Overview in his record names Dooley, Quaid and Oliveira.

candidates.name: Julian Goldie
candidates.statement: **Julian Goldie.** Self-declared, through a blog network and video reach.

candidates.name: Jacky Chou
candidates.statement: **Jacky Chou.** Entered 7 September (EVOIX); not in Oliveira's index.

candidates.name: Jesper Nissen; Edward Sturm
candidates.statement: **Not candidates.** Jesper Nissen, author of the fabricated coronation narrative. Edward Sturm, observer, through whose videos the assertion was first composed as an assertion.

round_constraints.title: Reading for development, in both directions of evaluation
round_constraints.source: the author, 2026-10-10 12:35 EDT: 'yes, lets work it into mantle-bearing, and kets attempt to add some constraints for reading developmental in both directions of evaluation'
round_constraints.status: in force for every round and every reading of a determination this dataset records, from 1.14; adoption into the packet (#1656) is the author's ruling
round_constraints.applies_to: a judgment for the work and a judgment against it; the claimant and every work it is compared with

constraints.name: Whole and in order
constraints.rule: Read the work in its order, through to the end. A reading that leaves a span unread names it, by its first and last words or its line numbers, and does not call itself complete or 'in sequence'.
constraints.origin: lee-sharks-experimental-poets-chatgpt-20261010: answer 5 announces 'the complete text' and leaves lines 25–48 (from 'I am a dinosaur…' to '…because babies are billionaires too…'), 24 of 77 unread

constraints.name: No opening as exemplar
constraints.rule: A device's first occurrence shows it at its introduction. A judgment of the device cites it at its first and its last occurrence and says what changed between them.
constraints.origin: lee-sharks-experimental-poets-chatgpt-20261010: answer 3 judges each movement by its first lines; the author: 'except you have not read it for development. you have collapsed the earliest, undeveloped points in each movement into exemplars of the whole. that is something you did, not a feature of the poem.'

constraints.name: Recurrence read before it is judged
constraints.rule: Where a word, image, line-form or grammar recurs, state its function at each occurrence before calling the recurrence repetition, accumulation or development.

constraints.name: First appearances located
constraints.rule: A claim that something returns, or is introduced, names its first occurrence by line.
constraints.origin: lee-sharks-experimental-poets-chatgpt-20261010: answer 5 places the first return of I AM at line 53 and introduces billionaire babies at lines 72–73; both occur first in lines 25 and 48

constraints.name: The work's own answer engaged
constraints.rule: Where the work stages, states or satirizes the charge a reading brings, the reading engages that passage before bringing the charge.

constraints.name: Both directions: for and against
constraints.rule: A judgment for the work carries the same requirements as a judgment against it. Praise of a device, like a fault found in it, cites the development it rests on; neither is entered as a finding without it.

substitution.origin: lee-sharks-experimental-poets-chatgpt-20261010; the author: 'you literally substituted accumulation for development as a reader then ascribed that operation to the poem as its primary vulnerability. read it for development.'
